newsitem.title: UK: Brazil CERJ sell-off a model for next sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CERJ sell-off a model for next sales.

text.p: The method used in the privatisation of Brazilian electric utility comany CERJ is likely to be applied in forthcoming sell-offs in the sector, a leading Brazilian investment bank said on Wednesday.

Banco de Investimentos Garantia SA, which led the consortium that advised Rio de Janeiro state on last week's successful CERJ sell-off, said the BNDES agency in charge of implementing Brazil's privatisations was keen to reapply the methodology.

"The BNDES (Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Economico e Social) and various state governments have already expressed interest in using this new privatisation methodology," Garantia said in a statement released in London.
"The successful sale of CERJ is expected to lead to additional privatisations of state government-owned electric utilities in Brazil."

Compania de Electricidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (CERJ) was sold on November 20 for $587 million -- a 30.3 percent premium over the minimum asking price -- to a consortium of investors led by Chile's Enersis SA.

The Garantia-led group introduced various changes to the privatisation process. It required potential buyers to submit sealed bids rather than conducting the sale by auction, and obliged each bidding group to include an electric power company operator among its investors.
The CERJ privatisation is the second-largest sell-off of an electric sector company in Brazil after the sale of Rio de Janeiro's Light in May, Garantia said.
Official figures quoted last June show Brazil's electricity sector has a net worth of about $20 billion after subtracting some $18 billion in debt.
Sao Paulo's electric firms account for $13-$14 billion of this, and the major players CESP, CPFL and Electropaulo have yet to go under the hammer.
Sao Paulo's power sector produces more electricity than Argentina and Chile combined. The state hopes to complete the sales during 1997.
